prompt: Fix split_fields(line): split on unescaped commas. A backslash escapes the next character (including comma or backslash); a final unmatched backslash is literal. Preserve empty fields and whitespace. Empty input means one empty field.
Repair next_month(date) for billing dates: move to the next calendar month, clamping the day to that month’s last day. Support leap years and December rollover; return a datetime.date.

Invoice totals lose cents. invoice_total(lines) receives (unit_price_string, integer_quantity) pairs. Round each extended line to cents with decimal ROUND_HALF_UP, then sum. Return Decimal with two decimal places, including for no lines. Negative lines are credits and use the same rounding rule.

Memo.get(key) should call its loader only on a cache miss. Cached None, False, zero, and empty strings are valid hits. A loader exception must propagate and must not cache a value; a later call can retry. clear() invalidates all keys.

Fix parse_args(argv), which returns (verbose, paths). Recognize -v and --verbose until the first standalone --. After that separator every token is a literal path, including another --. Before it, reject other dash-prefixed options except the literal stdin path -. Preserve path order and support options mixed with paths.

word_counts(text) should count case-insensitive Unicode words. Normalize text to NFC then casefold. A word is a maximal run of alphabetic characters or Unicode combining marks attached after a letter; digits, underscores, punctuation and whitespace separate words. Ignore unattached marks. Return a plain dict of counts.

merge_ranges(ranges) must merge overlapping or touching half-open numeric ranges, return sorted (start, end) tuples, and leave caller input unchanged. Ignore empty ranges (start == end). Raise ValueError for reversed ranges even if they would otherwise be swallowed by a larger range.

load_config(overrides) leaks changes between requests. Return a fresh deep copy of DEFAULTS with top-level overrides replacing entire values. Neither defaults nor any nested override objects may be shared with the returned config. None means no overrides; preserve falsey overrides and unknown keys.

Fix TTLCache using its injected clock. put(key, value, ttl) expires at clock()+ttl; get returns default when now >= expiry. Nonpositive TTL invalidates that key immediately. Missing/expired keys must not hide live falsey values, and reading must not extend expiry. Replacing a key resets its expiry.

PriorityQueue.push(priority, item) must accept arbitrary payloads, including dicts. pop() returns the lowest-priority payload, with FIFO order among equal priorities. len(queue) tracks pending items; an empty pop raises IndexError. Payloads must never need to be comparable.

read_records(text) mishandles CSV exports. Parse standard comma-separated CSV, including quoted commas, doubled quotes, and embedded newlines. The first nonblank record is the header; skip blank records, preserve field whitespace and empty fields, and return dict rows. Raise ValueError for duplicate headers or any data row with a different field count. Empty/blank-only input returns [].

run_with_retry(operation, attempts, retry_on, sleep) should make at most attempts total calls (attempts must be >= 1). Retry only exceptions matching retry_on, a tuple of exception classes. Sleep 1, 2, 4, ... seconds only between retries. Return successful values, including falsey ones; propagate the last exception unchanged when exhausted, and never sleep after the final attempt.

Fix lookup(data, path, default=None) for dotted paths through nested dictionaries and lists. Dictionary segments are literal keys, even numeric ones; list segments must contain only ASCII decimal digits and index from zero (leading zeros allowed). Missing keys, invalid/out-of-range indices, and traversal through scalars return default. Empty path returns the original data. Existing None/False values are valid results.

windows(iterable, size) should lazily yield overlapping full windows as tuples. Validate size > 0 with ValueError before consuming input. Consume exactly size elements for the first result, then one per subsequent result, and work with one-shot iterators. No partial windows; too-short input yields nothing.

Fix build_order(graph), where each mapping key is a job and its iterable value names prerequisites. Return every key and prerequisite-only job once, prerequisites first. At each step choose the lexicographically smallest currently ready job. Duplicate edges count once. Raise ValueError on any cycle (including disconnected cycles or self-loops), and never mutate graph or its lists.

Store.transaction() is a nested transaction context manager. On any BaseException leaving a block, restore the entire data dict (including nested mutable values) to its state when that block began and re-raise the same exception. Successful blocks keep changes. An inner rollback caught inside an outer transaction must preserve earlier outer changes, and an outer rollback must undo successful inner work. Keep store.data the same dict object for existing observers; nested object identities need not survive rollback.

Add encode_query(pairs) for ordered (key, value) pairs. Percent-encode UTF-8 keys and values using URL query rules (spaces become +). Preserve duplicate keys and order. Skip None values, stringify other values, and return an empty string when there are no emitted pairs. Keep append_query behavior for existing encoded strings.

Add batches(iterable, size), a lazy iterator of independent lists of up to size elements, including a final short batch. Work with one-shot iterators and consume no more than one batch before yielding it. Reject nonpositive size with ValueError before consuming input. Empty input produces no batches.

Implement unique_slug(title, used). Normalize title with NFKD, drop non-ASCII characters, lowercase, replace each run of non-alphanumeric characters with a hyphen, and trim hyphens. Use "item" if empty. If taken, try base-2, base-3, etc. and return the first free slug without changing used. Treat used slugs as exact, case-sensitive strings.

Implement group_rows(rows, key), returning a list of (group_value, rows_in_group) tuples in order of each group’s first appearance. Within groups preserve row order and original row objects. Missing key and explicit None belong to one None group; other falsey keys remain distinct according to normal Python equality. Consume an iterable once and do not mutate rows. Group values are hashable.

Implement merge_patch(target, patch) with JSON merge-patch semantics: a non-dict patch replaces the whole target; a dict patch merges recursively into a dict target (or an empty dict for a non-dict target); None-valued members delete keys. Lists replace rather than merge. Never mutate either input, and return data with no mutable containers shared with either input, including untouched branches.

Add add_business_days(start, offset, holidays=()). Move forward or backward by an integer number of business days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and supplied date holidays. Do not count the starting date. Offset zero returns start unchanged even on a holiday/weekend. Do not alter holidays; support date boundaries and leap days.

Implement LRUCache(capacity), with positive integer capacity (nonpositive raises ValueError), get(key, default=None), put(key, value), and len(cache). Successful get and every put make a key most recently used. Missing gets do not affect recency. Inserting beyond capacity evicts the least recently used key; overwrites do not grow the cache. Falsey values are valid.

Add reservations to Inventory. Initial stock maps SKU to nonnegative integers. reserve(token, items) takes nonnegative integer quantities: atomically subtract all if available, otherwise raise ValueError (also for unknown SKUs or negative quantities). A repeated active token with the same items is an idempotent no-op; different items raise ValueError. release(token) restores stock once and returns True, or False if unknown/already released. available(sku) returns stock or zero. Defensively copy stock and reservation inputs. Released tokens may be reused.

Implement resolve_config(values) for a mapping of string keys to strings. Expand ${name} references recursively, regardless of key order. $$ emits a literal dollar and must not start a reference (so $${x} becomes literal ${x}); inserted results are not scanned again. A lone dollar is literal. Empty values are valid. Raise ValueError for unknown references, unclosed ${...}, or any reference cycle, including unused/disconnected cycles. Return a new dict without mutating input. Reference names are the exact text between braces.

Implement Router.add(pattern, handler) and match(path). Patterns and paths start with /, split into slash-separated segments, and ignore trailing slashes; / has no segments. Patterns allow literal segments, :name for exactly one nonempty segment, and final *name for zero or more remaining segments joined by /. Names must be nonempty and unique in a pattern; nonfinal wildcards are invalid (ValueError). match returns (handler, captured_dict) or None. Choose the matching route with the lexicographically highest sequence of segment specificity (literal=2, parameter=1, wildcard=0); if tied, earlier registration wins. An exact route beats its own wildcard extension when the wildcard captures zero segments. Do not decode or normalize other path contents.

Unify the temperature conversions behind convert(value, source, target), supporting case-insensitive C, F and K codes. Keep c_to_f and f_to_c callable with their existing results, and have them use the shared conversion behavior. Add Kelvin support and identity conversions. Unknown units raise ValueError. Do not reject negative temperatures or round outputs.

Refactor sales_total(rows) and sales_by_region(rows) to share the same row interpretation. Preserve existing sale behavior: rows have region and integer amount, missing kind means sale. Add kind="refund", which subtracts amount, and kind="void", which is ignored even if region/amount are missing. Unknown kinds raise ValueError. Keep zero-total regions, preserve region first-seen order among nonvoid rows, accept one-shot iterables, and do not mutate rows.

Refactor the report exporters to share render(rows, format, columns). Keep as_json(rows) and as_text(rows, columns) byte-for-byte compatible: JSON uses sort_keys=True; text emits tab-joined columns with missing values empty, one line per row, no trailing newline. Add render formats json, text, csv (unknown format raises ValueError). CSV includes a header even with no rows, uses CRLF record endings and standard CSV quoting, writes None/missing as empty, and follows columns order. JSON ignores columns. Support one-shot row iterables.

Refactor validate_user and validate_team to share validation rules while keeping their current list-of-error-codes API and error ordering (name first, count second). Names must now be strings with non-whitespace content; strip only for checking, without mutating data. Counts must be nonnegative ints and must reject bool (Python otherwise treats bool as int). Add validate_project using title/seats fields and error codes title_required, seats_invalid. Missing fields are invalid; extra fields are ignored.

Refactor Job.send(event) around a single transition definition, preserving new -> running on start, running -> done on finish, and new/running -> cancelled on cancel. Add pause from running -> paused, resume from paused -> running, and cancel from paused -> cancelled. Invalid events raise ValueError without changing state/history. Each successful event appends (old_state, event, new_state) to history. done and cancelled are terminal. Keep initial state new and an independent history per instance.

Replace evaluate(text)’s ad hoc arithmetic handling with a structured parser while preserving sums/subtractions of nonnegative integers. Add multiplication, true division, parentheses, and unary +/-. Use ordinary precedence (unary, then */ left-to-right, then +- left-to-right); allow repeated unary signs and arbitrary whitespace between tokens. Numbers are ASCII nonnegative integer literals (no decimals). Reject empty input, invalid characters, missing operands, unbalanced parentheses, adjacent numbers, and trailing tokens with ValueError. Division by zero raises ZeroDivisionError. Do not execute input as Python.

Wire configurable request timeouts through settings.py and cli.py. load_settings(mapping) returns a Settings whose timeout defaults to 30.0; accept numeric values or numeric strings strictly greater than zero and finite, otherwise ValueError (including bool). parse_cli(argv, defaults=None) returns Settings, using defaults as the settings mapping, with an optional --timeout VALUE overriding it. Last repeated option wins. Missing values or unknown arguments raise ValueError. Keep Settings.retries=3 and describe() output working. Both direct loading and CLI overrides must use the same timeout validation.

Add tags to Record and its JSON storage. Record(id, text, tags=()) must store an independent list of unique tags in first-seen order, trimming whitespace and dropping empty tags; preserve case. dumps(records) writes version 2 with tags for each record. loads(text) accepts version 1 (tags omitted, default empty) and version 2 (tags required), rejects unknown versions with ValueError, and returns Records using the same normalization. Keep id/text round-trips and record_count working. Do not mutate input tag lists.

Upgrade the byte protocol in codec.py and stream.py. A frame is a two-byte unsigned big-endian payload length, the payload (0..65535 bytes), then a one-byte checksum equal to sum(payload)%256. encode(payload) returns a frame and rejects oversized payloads with ValueError. decode(frame) requires exactly one complete frame and validates length/checksum, otherwise ValueError. FrameReader.feed(chunk) accepts arbitrary byte chunks, buffers incomplete data, and returns all newly completed payloads in order (including empty payloads); finish() raises ValueError for a truncated tail and otherwise returns None. A malformed completed frame clears buffered data and raises ValueError; the reader must then accept a fresh valid stream. Returned payloads are bytes.

Add exact-cent money handling and atomic transfers across money.py and ledger.py. to_cents(value) accepts decimal strings or Decimal, rounds half-up to cents (including negative halves), returns int, and raises ValueError for invalid/nonfinite values. format_cents(int) returns a signed decimal string with two places. Ledger(opening) converts each opening balance with to_cents and rejects negative balances. balance(account) returns formatted money and raises KeyError for unknown accounts. transfer(source, target, amount) converts amount once, rejects nonpositive rounded amounts with ValueError, checks both accounts (KeyError) and sufficient funds (ValueError), then updates atomically. A self-transfer still validates amount/accounts/funds but leaves balance unchanged. Never mutate opening.

Complete encode_runs(values) and decode_runs(runs) to satisfy the supplied behavioral tests. encode_runs returns (value, count) tuples for consecutive equal values, preserving order (do not combine separated runs). Values can be unhashable. decode_runs returns the expanded list; counts must be positive ints, excluding bool, otherwise ValueError. Both accept one-shot iterables and empty input; neither mutates input.

Implement histogram(values, edges) from the supplied tests. For n strictly increasing numeric edges return n+1 counts: below edge[0], then half-open intervals [edge[i], edge[i+1]), then values >= the last edge. With no edges every value belongs to the single bin. Values/edges contain finite numbers. Reject duplicate or unsorted edges with ValueError, do not mutate inputs, and support one-shot values iterators.

Implement SuggestionIndex according to the tests. add(word) increments a word’s frequency; remove(word) removes one occurrence and returns True, or False if absent. suggest(prefix, limit=5) returns distinct words starting with prefix, ranked by descending frequency then lexicographically, truncated to limit. Zero limit returns []; negative limit raises ValueError. Matching is case-sensitive, empty words/prefixes are supported, and returned lists must be independent snapshots.

Implement shortest_path(graph, start, end) to satisfy the provided tests. graph maps string node names to dictionaries of neighbor names and nonnegative integer edge costs; neighbor-only nodes exist too. Return (total_cost, list_of_nodes) for the best directed path, or None if either endpoint is absent or no path exists. Among equal-cost paths choose fewer edges, then the lexicographically smallest complete node sequence. A known node to itself returns (0, [node]). Validate the entire graph and raise ValueError for any negative cost, even in unreachable components. Handle zero-cost cycles without looping and never mutate graph.
